A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyGen and provide readable main text, figures, equations and complete appendices. Their methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial rewriting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original trace-driven latency and throughput experiments, predictor-accuracy measurements, prefix-sharing simulations and ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds offline-capacity comparisons, an A5000/Sheared-LLaMA-2.7B experiment and further workload characterization.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes decode admission from a latency-budget condition to allowing online decoding regardless of the remaining budget. V1's fairness-aware PSM is retained as v4 Algorithm 4; separately documenting basic PSM does not introduce a new policy. A predictor feature change remains unresolved: v4 Equation 1 retains S_d², while Appendix B's Equation 2 omits it.

E1.justification: Azure and Mooncake online traces, arXiv and CNN/DailyMail summarization, and the MMLU prefix-sharing simulation already appear in v1. V4 retains this coverage. The added hardware/model configuration changes experimental settings; MoE and Mamba are discussed without evaluation.

E2.justification: V1 Figure 4 compares HyGen with HyGen*. V4 adds Sarathi and the newly evaluated, chunk-size-tuned Sarathi-offline comparator. Sarathi also joins the retained Yi-34B, CNN/DailyMail and Mooncake throughput comparisons. The existing latency and prefix-sharing comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Figure 4 and several throughput ablations change their reported metric from offline TPS to total TPS, substantially broadening the central evaluation to overall serving efficiency. V4 also introduces chunk-size optimization for Sarathi-offline and an A5000 with 24GB VRAM/Sheared-LLaMA-2.7B setting. Existing trace subsampling, latency metrics and prefix-sharing simulation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds a hardware/model-size ablation testing SLO compliance and throughput on the A5000/2.7B configuration, plus Mooncake arrival-rate characterization over two timescales. The existing predictor, profiler, prefix-sharing, parallelism, SLO and arrival-rate analyses remain after matching their renumbered figures.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty error bars. Means, P99 latencies and predictor-error CDFs retain the same descriptive reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 substantially expands throughput results through total-TPS curves and added comparator entries. Section 5.2 newly reports up to 3.87× total throughput over pure online serving and 84.3% of Sarathi-offline throughput; Figure 15 adds reported gains of 2.18× offline and 1.30× overall throughput. The 5.84× offline gain and predictor MAPEs of 1.78%/1.07% are retained. Offline-to-total conversions do not establish same-metric performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 analyzes constant-time prediction, trie construction and updates, freshness-tree operations, and an O(n) scheduling path using asynchronous maintenance. V1 has no corresponding complexity analysis. V4 does not supply a fairness theorem or proof despite newly claiming theoretical fairness guarantees.

C1.justification: The central claim of improved throughput while preserving online SLOs remains. V4 expands the headline comparison to online and hybrid baselines, reporting 3.87–5.84× gains, and newly describes its scheduling contribution as constrained optimization with theoretical fairness guarantees. These strengthen particular contribution claims without changing the central research objective.

C2.justification: V4 adds specific limitations concerning predictor instability, single-model scope and workload generalization. Appendices B–C introduce substantive arguments about profiler-mediated robustness, applicability to MoE/hybrid architectures and complementarity with instance scaling. Conversely, v1's explicit qualification that online priority can still starve offline requests is omitted.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code release to reporting a public repository, substantially changing documented access information. V4 also adds licenses, asynchronous DFS-list/FCFS-queue implementation details, explicit hardware information for added tests and approximately 18-microsecond predictor runtime. Some v1 hardware specifics, including CPU model and SMT configuration, are removed. Repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially repositions HyGen against predictive scheduling and shared-prefix inference, while the main text and appendices add routing and autoscaling context. New citations include Hydragen, RouteLLM, InferCept, Preble and ServerlessLLM. Much of v1's cache-management, quantization and generic co-location survey is removed, including InfiniGen and NanoFlow.

P1.justification: Sections 2–4 undergo substantial rewriting: background shifts toward serving instances, the scheduling overview becomes explicit phases, predictor training explanations are condensed, and PSM gains worked request-order examples. The appendix separates basic and fairness-aware PSM and adds dedicated complexity, predictor and deployment discussions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure regrouping and relocation. Figure 2 is redrawn to expose latency prediction and successive offline additions; throughput plots gain total-TPS axes and comparator curves. New Mooncake-characterization and A5000 figures appear, and algorithm displays are expanded and restyled.

improvement.justification: V4 makes the efficiency argument easier to assess through pure-online/pure-offline throughput references and the smaller-GPU experiment, while stated code access and explicit limitations improve reuse and scope clarity. These provide a limited net quality gain. New unsupported theoretical-fairness claims and inconsistent predictor feature lists in Equations 1–2 weaken precision and prevent a stronger improvement judgment.
